\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize\setstretch{1.0}\emph{Notes.} Each walk-forward design picks, in every training window, the rule with the highest Sharpe ratio among the 351 rules of Table~1 and trades it over the next test block. The test is whether the strategy beats buy-and-hold (returns above T-bills), with Newey--West $t$-statistics. $p$ naive treats the best design as if it were the only one tried; max-$t$ is the studentised Reality Check over the 56 designs; avg-$t$ tests the average $t$-statistic across all designs, with critical values from the stationary bootstrap (1,999 draws). Signif.\ counts designs with naive $p<0.05$ and with Romano--Wolf StepM adjusted $p<0.05$. Corr.\ is the mean pairwise correlation of the 56 daily series of strategy minus buy-and-hold returns and Eff.\ no.\ the participation-ratio effective number of designs computed from it. PBO is the probability of backtest overfitting from 16-block combinatorially symmetric cross-validation. In Panel C a signal at the close of day $t$ is traded at the close of day $t+1$, in the training windows and in the test blocks. Bold: $p<0.05$.
\end{minipage}
